$comment: CW3 language-neutral drift fixture for validate_item — the ONE pin holding the three implementations together: aidream/services/cms/collection_validation.py (CANONICAL, Python), my-matrx/lib/collections/validateItem.js (visitor path, JS), and matrx-frontend/features/cms/collections/validateItem.ts (admin path, TS). All three run every case byte-identically. expect.rejected_fields / expect.warning_fields are SORTED, DEDUPED key lists. expect.rejected_issues / expect.warning_issues are SORTED lists of [key, code] pairs, NOT deduped — they pin the error-code vocabulary AND the issue multiplicity, which bare field lists are structurally blind to (that blindness is how Python's coarse 'constraint_violation' code and its short-circuit-after-first-failure both survived undetected). Codes: required_missing | unknown_key | type_mismatch | max_length | out_of_range | invalid_option; the issue's identifier property is 'key' on all three. utf8_byte_length_cases / item_byte_size_cases pin the caller-enforced byte-cap counters (UTF-8 bytes; item bytes = compact JSON, no ascii escaping). max_length counts Unicode CODE POINTS (JS: [...s].length, NEVER .length). required constrains ONLY when it is the literal boolean true.

validate_cases.name: combining_marks_count_as_separate_code_points
validate_cases.$comment: e + U+0301 combining acute = 2 code points, over max_length 1
